contract: GET /auth/openid/config. Authenticated admin discovery requires issuer and returns the provider discovery document or a client-visible failure; anonymous users receive 401 and non-admins 403.

invariants.contract: GET /auth/openid/config requires a bearer token: an anonymous caller gets 401 and an ordinary user gets 403, and neither answer contains the configured client id/secret, issuer URL or an internal trace. An admin call must pass a string issuer, else 400. The issuer loses one trailing slash and is fetched at <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration; success answers 200 with exactly issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, userinfo_endpoint, end_session_endpoint, jwks_uri and id_token_signing_alg_values_supported copied from that document (the document's code_challenge_methods_supported is not forwarded). An unparseable issuer, an issuer whose well-known URL does not end in the configuration document (for example one carrying a query), a document answering 404 and an unreachable issuer answer 400 without provider detail.
exceptions: Only the access rule, the seven forwarded fields and the failure statuses are asserted; the HTML/text of the 401/403 bodies is free.
Mapping note: the named internal Go test is an assertion lead only; the shared scenarios are the executable oracle.
The admin settings endpoint that might expose the same provider fields (PATCH /api/auth-settings) is owned by the admin_settings packet; this requirement asserts only the discovery route.
